newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RTZ-CRA sees strong China zinc exports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RTZ-CRA sees strong China zinc exports.

text.p: RTZ-CRA said on Monday it expects Chinese exports of zinc to remain strong at about 200,000 tonnes a year over the next few years.

"If prices were to rise substantially they would probably exceed the present forecast," Phillip Crowson, the Anglo-Australian mining giant's chief economist, told a metals industry conference in Melbourne.
However, inventories of zinc on a world scale were in decline following a swelling to peak levels in 1994 when the stock-to-consumption ratio exceeded three months, he said.
"By the end of this year they will be down to a more reasonable level of about eight weeks demand," Crowson said.
He said eight weeks demand still represented a high ratio when compared with the average of the 1980s.
The fall in stocks had not been confined to inventories held in London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouses, although LME zinc stocks represented over half the world inventory total, he said.
